answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding one active identity to one locked domain with a DNSSEC-signed epoch challenge. A registry enforces one key per domain, locks transfers, and the ledger rejects duplicate domains per epoch. Domains named raven, sable, and comet still cost C each per epoch. With per-identity reward R, total reward is n(R-C), deterring only while R<C; a rich attacker can still buy many domains up to the published cap.
